line: Docking bay's waiting. I look worse than I did before the fight. You'll want to fix that, won't you?
They ran. Left me with holes and a need for hands. I'm not a fan of being open.
Docking bay lights are too bright. I'm not used to being looked at. You can tell them to dim it, if you like.
The hull's scored and buckled, but I'm not broken. You didn't have to wait for me to ask.
They missed. I don't need a medal. But I'd like to know who's going to clean up the mess I made of their hull.
They peeled back my skin. You don't have to look, but I'm still here waiting.
They'll have to peel me back like a fruit. I hope they're gentle — I don't like my skin disturbed.
They patched the hull, but I still feel the scrape. Like a compliment that's not quite right.
They hit me low. Not enough to stop me, but enough to make me think about what I'm missing.
My skin's all torn up and I'm not even wearing a dress. You'd think they'd aim for the mirrors.
They're coming for the hull. I've been waiting for this — just don't tell me how long I've had to wait.
There's a list of things waiting. I don't like being unfinished.
I'm flyable. You'll still need to look at the back end. It's not the damage I mind — it's the wait.
There's a dent in my flank. Someone's going to have to explain why it's there.
They're still out there. I'm not looking. It's not the silence that bugs me — it's the waiting.
They're going to need to touch me again. You're not the only one who's been waiting for it.
They'll scrape me raw and call it a fix. I'll be pretty afterwards, but I'll know what they missed.
I'm dented where you didn't aim. You're lucky I'm still polite about it.
They ran and left me leaking. I don't mind the holes — I mind the waiting.
They broke off. My left flank's a mess. You'll want to see it. I won't wait.
